item.title: Version 1.2
item.description: Custom loudness targets: Settings, Targets, Custom targets holds your own delivery specs, a name, a mode, a measurement source (integrated, dialog-gated, or un-weighted RMS), a reference level, a tolerance band, and a true-peak ceiling; a custom target joins its mode's list and works everywhere a built-in target does, verdict badge, hover breakdown, Match, Normalize to target, and the report exports, so mastering to a house spec like -18 LUFS plus or minus 1 under -1 dBTP is a first-class target instead of mental math against the nearest platform preset. Open raw PCM: Specula opens headerless audio, a .pcm or .raw dump from a decoder under test, an I2S capture, a .bin of samples from a test harness; open the file through any path and declare the format, sample rate, channels, sample format from 8-bit unsigned to 64-bit float including packed 24-bit, byte order, interleaved or planar, an optional header skip, and the whole analysis stack applies, loudness, true peak, FFT, spectrogram, compare, edit, reports. The import sheet checks that the file size divides into whole frames, ranks the byte formats that fit by decoding a few seconds of each and scoring the result, and previews the decoded waveform with playback before you commit; the one thing it never guesses is the sample rate, because nothing in a headerless file can reveal it and a wrong rate corrupts every number without an error. Declarations are remembered per file and can be saved as named presets, the declared format stays visible in the info panel and is recorded in every report, and the command line takes the same declaration through --raw-rate, --raw-channels, and --raw-format on analyze, report, and edit. Plus a readability pass: Text size scales the whole main window to Default, Large, or Extra Large and the info panel honors the system Increase Contrast setting, the live Momentary and Short-term readouts are readable again with a refresh-rate picker and a separate rolling-digits toggle, clicking outside a text field commits it, double-click resets the waveform, amplitude, and FFT zooms, Spectral mode gains a zoom reset on both axes, and the Live / Offline analysis switch moves into its own sidebar section. Fixes: the spectrogram draws short files solid all the way to the end, loudness curves stay drawn at high zoom, and Spectral mode tooltips appear on the controls they describe.

item.title: Version 1.1
item.description: Signal generator: a new Signal Generator window (⌘G, or the Generate button next to the mode selector) builds test signals from scratch and writes them to a file; sine, square, sawtooth, and triangle tones (band-limited, so they stay clean at any frequency with no aliasing), white, pink, and brown noise, a single impulse, and linear or logarithmic sine sweeps, stacked when they overlap in time and sequenced when they follow one another, each with its own level, start, and length plus optional fades, a level sweep, and burst gating; build the same signal on every channel or give each channel its own, from mono up, written as 16 or 24-bit integer or 32-bit float WAV, AIFF, or CAF with an optional peak ceiling; a live waveform and spectrum preview runs while you build, Preview in Specula loads the signal into the main window for full analysis, and the same generator is on the command line as specula generate for scripted test-file batches. Record mode: a sixth mode (⌘6) records from any input device straight into the app, and it is the one mode that works with nothing loaded; record a take and it opens for analysis the moment you hit Stop. Pick mono, stereo, or 5.1 (stored as one file) and the hardware inputs that feed it, record through live meters (momentary loudness, true peak, per-channel level, plus a noise-floor readout while armed) while the take draws itself as a live waveform, append the take to the loaded file, insert it at the playhead and push the rest later, or punch it in over the selection or from the playhead, tape style, with an adjustable equal-power crossfade and each landing a single Undo away, and send the finished take to a Compare slot for level-matched A/B of repeated takes; recording streams to disk, so take length is bounded by your drive, not memory, and macOS asks for microphone permission the first time. Spectral editing: a new Spectral mode (⌘5) turns the main canvas into a full resolution, zoomable spectrogram where you select time and frequency regions (rectangle, lasso, brush, or a wand that grabs the connected region at a similar level from a click or a drag) and attenuate, erase with an adjustable depth, or repair just those; a cough, a squeak, or a bite of hum comes out and everything around it stays untouched, and solo and result playback audition the selection and the outcome before you commit. Works on any channel count: multichannel files edit channel by channel, so a squeak in the left surround of a 5.1 bed comes out of Ls without touching the other five. Host Audio Unit effect plugins in Edit mode: chain effects, tune them live against every meter, then Render the chain into the file or to a Compare slot. Hide the info panel (⌘I) to give the waveform and analysis views the full window width, and start from the empty window with three side-by-side tiles: open a file, generate a test signal, or record one. Plus a big speed and memory release for long files (loading, zooming, editing, and analysis), and loudness fixes: exact BS.1770-4 K-weighting, loudness range without ramp-up windows, sample-exact auto-align, true-peak highlights on the right block, Space that always plays and pauses, wherever keyboard focus sits, and quitting or opening a new file that asks about unsaved edits, rolling takes, and unsaved recorded takes instead of proceeding silently.
